title: Chat Completions Interop Normalizer: OpenAI request/response mapping shim
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Implement a normalization shim that translates Redwood's native chat streaming and function/tool calling payloads to the OpenAI Chat Completions request/response shape (and vice versa) to support legacy customer integrations. This ticket covers the mapping layer, edge-case handling for streamed deltas (role/name changes, incremental function_call arguments), structured output enforcement (JSON schema hooks), fallbacks when models emit non-OpenAI semantics, and a safe rollout strategy.

Goals: keep latency and throughput within current SLOs, preserve token-level streaming experience for consumers expecting OpenAI-style deltas, and provide a compatibility toggle header for customers to opt into the shim.

Design highlights: translate Redwood streaming frames to OpenAI-style "delta" objects with fields: role, content, function_call.name, function_call.arguments (incremental). For tool/function calls we will aggregate partial argument fragments during streaming and emit a final function_call object at end, while also exposing intermediate partials via an opt-in streaming flag. Structured outputs will be validated against supplied JSON schemas and non-conforming outputs will be annotated with an errors array in the final delta. Fallback policy: when runtime detects incompatible model output (e.g., proprietary chunking), route to a slow-path translator that rebuilds messages and re-serializes to OpenAI shape; emit telemetry and backpressure if translation latency > 150ms.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict compatibility mode increases CPU/memory due to buffering streamed fragments; mitigated by a configurable buffer size and a per-request compatibility flag.
- Aggressive validation of structured outputs can surface false positives for model creativity; will default to warning mode unless customer opts into enforcement.

Deliverables: schema mapping code, unit + integration tests, PR for API docs updates, console flag in Redwood Console to enable compatibility per org, rollout plan with canary percent and metrics to watch (errors/unit, P95 tail latency, function_call completeness).
acceptance_criteria: Requests with header X-Compat: openai return OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 shaped responses for text and streaming endpoints
Streamed deltas include role/name/content increments matching OpenAI delta semantics
Function/tool calls streamed incrementally and final function_call.arguments aggregated correctly in >= 99% test cases
Structured output validation runs without increasing P95 server-side latency by more than 10% in canary
Integration tests added for edge cases: role flips mid-stream, interleaved function_call fragments, non-UTF8 token input
comments: 2025-03-10 Ava Chen: Initial ticket created after sync with PM and Runtime team. Key ask: support customers who expect OpenAI chat streaming semantics without changing Redwood runtime internals.
2025-03-11 Diego Morales: Spike completed — implemented prototype normalizer in runtime proxy. Observed 120-180ms median translation cost for long streams; buffer tuning required.

2025-03-12 Priya Patel (PM) : Reviewed trade-offs. PM prefers opt-in compatibility toggle per-organization rather than global default. Requested metrics: function_call-completeness, schema-violations, and additional telemetry for partial argument reassembly.
2025-03-14 Ramon Alvarez (SRE): Raised concern about memory pressure under high concurrency. Proposed per-request streaming buffer cap and circuit-breaker when memory exceeds threshold.
2025-03-15 Diego Morales: Implemented incremental buffer cap and slow-path translator. Added metrics and a feature flag. Preparing PR.

2025-03-16 Design review comments from Elena Park: Suggested adding example mappings in docs for common failure modes and explicit guidance for customers using function calling with tools that stream binary payloads.

2025-03-17 Diego Morales: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/6132 for the mapping layer, draft console UI updates at https://drive.google.com/example-doc and integration test harness at https://github.com/redwood-inference/integration-tests/pull/128
